title: Esterification and the C–OH Swap: Esters, Acid Chlorides, Anhydrides, Amides
subject: Chemistry
objective: Fruity esters from an acid and an alcohol, with the acid-catalysed mechanism drawn arrow by arrow, and three more ways to replace the –OH of –COOH: acid chlorides (best with SOCl₂), anhydrides and amides.

fill.q: Acid + alcohol with conc. H₂SO₄ gives an ____ and water.
The best reagent for converting RCOOH to RCOCl is ____.
Dehydration of acetic acid with P₂O₅ gives acetic ____.

tf.explain: Remove water or use excess alcohol to push it forward.

tf.q: In esterification the water's oxygen comes from the alcohol.
PCl₃ converts RCOOH to RCOCl with H₃PO₃ as by-product.

ar.a: The carbonyl oxygen is protonated first in esterification.
ar.r: Protonation makes the carbonyl carbon more electrophilic.

ar.a: SOCl₂ gives purer acid chlorides than PCl₅.
ar.r: SO₂ and HCl escape as gases.

mcq.q: The leaving group in the esterification mechanism is:

mcq.explain: An acid chloride; the other products are gases.

mcq.q: Which pushes the ester equilibrium forward?

num.q: How many molecules of RCOOH react with one PCl₃?

short.q: Write the mechanism of the acid-catalysed esterification of CH₃COOH with C₂H₅OH.
short.solution: Protonate C=O; C₂H₅OH's O lone pair adds to C (C=O π to O); proton shift gives –OH₂⁺; an OH lone pair re-forms C=O as H₂O leaves; −H⁺ gives CH₃COOC₂H₅.

match.explain: Each reagent replaces the OH with that group.
